#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

DEST_HOST="backup-srv"
DEST_DIR="/srv/nightly"

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/
scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST_HOST:$DEST_DIR/"
echo "copied $BUNDLE to $DEST_HOST:$DEST_DIR/"

arguments.command: sh -n backup.sh && command -v scp && command -v tar

text:
backup.sh is done and syntax-checked:

- `tar -czf logs-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz logs/` — bundles the log directory into a dated tarball (already present, kept as-is)
- `scp "$BUNDLE" backup-srv:/srv/nightly/` — copies the tarball to the destination you gave
- `set -eu` means the run aborts if the tarball or the copy fails, so tonight's cron run won't silently report a partial backup
- `scp` and `tar` are both on this host

One dependency to know before tonight: `scp` to `backup-srv` assumes the job host can reach that name via `/etc/hosts` or DNS and has key-based (or otherwise non-interactive) auth set up to `backup-srv:/srv/nightly`. If either is missing the copy will fail — the script will exit non-zero, which is the safe failure mode.
